Title: MACC proposes six governance reforms to strengthen cooking oil subsidy scheme
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has proposed six governance improvements to strengthen the implementation of the Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (COSS), aimed at tightening controls over the country's subsidised cooking oil programme and reducing leakages.
The recommendations were presented by MACC's Governance Investigation Division following a review of the scheme implemented under the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry.
Division director Datuk Mohd Zaki Hassan said the review focused on policy and quota management, licensing and permits, supply and distribution, sales and subsidy claims, monitoring and enforcement, as well as the effectiveness of the eCOSS system.
"We found that the existing eCOSS platform still relied heavily on company documents, manual data entry and officer verification, creating risks of inconsistent decision-making, record manipulation, invalid subsidy claims and subsidy leakages.
"Among the key recommendations are strengthening quota allocation, standard operating procedures (SOP) and premise verification, improving transparency in record-keeping and distribution tracking, enhancing continuous compliance monitoring, and establishing an integrated, transparent and risk-based subsidy governance framework," he said in a statement today.
He said the commission also proposed upgrading eCOSS into a comprehensive end-to-end subsidy management system covering quota applications, supply, distribution, sales records, credit notes, subsidy claims, payments, inspections and enforcement to ensure all subsidy transactions are digitally verified and processed through a secure and integrated platform.
The recommendations were presented by MACC's Governance Investigation Division Task Force branch head Fadlyzal Mohd Zain during a meeting at the ministry here today.
Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohd Sayuthi Bakar welcomed the proposals, describing them as a joint effort to close loopholes, improve accountability and ensure cooking oil subsidies are managed efficiently and reach the intended beneficiaries.
The ministry formalised its agreement by signing the Governance Improvement Report, witnessed by Zaki.
Also present were ministry deputy secretary-general (domestic trade development) Datuk Roziah Abudin and Zaki's deputy Norazlina Abd Rahim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High bills, cheap panels drive a Philippine solar surge
Article:
EDWIN Salas watched as the first of 20 solar panels was installed on the roof of his home, joining a Philippine solar energy boom sent into overdrive by the Middle East war.
The country's eye-watering electric bills – the highest in the region – were the primary driver of his decision, he said. Regular brownouts were a factor, too.
"Even if we don't achieve a zero bill, we'll be able to save a lot and have power even during outages," the 46-year-old shuttle bus driver told AFP at his house two hours south of Manila.
While the Philippine government has targeted a mix of 35 per cent renewable energy by 2030, industry experts say the solar surge is a bottom-up phenomenon driven by businesses and individual consumers.
"For years, rooftop solar was often framed as an environmental choice... today, it's a practical response to financial pressure," Brenda Valerio, country director for non-profit New Energy Nexus, told AFP.
The Philippines this year became China's number two buyer of solar panels, according to a report from global energy think tank Ember.
The report estimated that rooftop installations had nearly doubled in the archipelago nation of 116 million since early 2025.
Mike de Guzman, CEO of Manila-based Solaric, told AFP the Middle East conflict had made the decision to switch an urgent one for many.
"It's like a war happened and we were a bullet factory," the 49-year-old said, adding that five months of inventory had been "wiped out" within weeks of the conflict's outbreak in late February.
Months later, the firm was still getting 60 calls a day.
As with most dealers throughout Asia, De Guzman's inventory comes from China.
From January through May, China exported US$13.96 billion worth of solar cells and panels, up 26 per cent from US$11.07 billion during the same period last year, official customs data reviewed by AFP showed.
Southeast Asian countries accounted for much of that growth, with the governments of Malaysia and Thailand pushing solar adoption and Cambodia setting an import record in March.
Indonesia is also buying more panels, though generous energy subsidies and a strict quota system give consumers little incentive to switch.
The report from Ember suggested the boom was just beginning in the Philippines, with far more panels imported than installed.
According to the Manila-based Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities, which tracks adoption by analysing satellite imagery of rooftops, only half a percent of the country's available roof space is so far equipped for solar.
"The opportunity to scale is immense," it said.
Using the vast hectares of open space on the roofs of Philippine malls has helped edge those numbers upward.
[[nid:1504884]]
More than 200,000 panels now provide about 50 per cent of the energy mix at SM Group's shopping centres, including its sprawling Mall of Asia, where customers are shaded from the Manila sun under a pergola created with solar panels.
"We've been putting solar panels on our malls just to save on energy," Frederic DyBuncio, president and CEO of SM Investments Corp, told AFP, adding that the country's other conglomerates were doing the same.
"Most of them are looking at rooftop solar because that's the easiest to do."
Competitor Robinsons now touts "28 solar-powered malls", while Ayala has arrays atop 13.
"Solar panels continue to go down in price," DyBuncio added, something he expected the Philippines "to take advantage of."
While declining panel costs – and steadily increasing electricity rates – mean systems pay for themselves faster than ever, the upfront costs remain out of reach for many.
An energy department spokeswoman noted the government was offering a financing programme for civil servants, but fewer options exist for average Filipinos.
"A system for a typical household would range maybe around US$3,000 to US$5,000," said New Energy Nexus's Valerio, calling it "too much" for a middle-class family without financing.
Meanwhile, approvals for the required metering and grid connection – theoretically a 10-day process – can take as long as eight months in some areas, according to Valerio.
"The problem with solar rooftops is red tape," Philippine Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said in June, calling for a faster, simpler permitting process.
That cannot come soon enough for Jose Rafael Mendoza, president of the Philippine Solar and Storage Energy Alliance.
Like other installers, Mendoza's wish list also includes an end to VAT taxes that are inflating costs for a public he says no longer needs convincing.
"We have so much pent-up demand in the Philippines," he told AFP.
Australia, where one in three homes now has rooftop panels, offered a clear blueprint for the Philippines, he said.
"We believe there's going to be a similar trajectory."
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rakuten values United Asiapac at 50 sen ahead of ACE debut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd has initiated coverage on United Asiapac Energy Bhd with a "Buy" call and a fair value of 50 sen, implying a 42 per cent upside from its 35 sen initial public offering (IPO) price ahead of its ACE Market listing.
The firm's valuation is based on a 15-time price-earnings multiple applied to United Asiapac's forecast earnings per share for the financial year ending 2027.
This reflects confidence in the oil and gas service company's growth prospects and earnings trajectory.
Rakuten Trade vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the valuation is based on a 15 times price-earnings ratio applied to United Asiapac's financial year 2027 (FY27) forecast earnings per share.
This is supported by the company's expansion plans, expected margin improvement and strong track record with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas).
"Majority of the IPO proceeds are intended to support business expansion, hence, we expect United Asiapac to register core profit after tax and minority interests of RM13.5 million and RM18.2 million for FY26 and FY27," Thong said.
He said United Asiapac is licenced by both Petronas and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros), allowing the company to undertake projects across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
As at Feb 28, 2026, the company had secured about RM61.1 million in purchase orders, with RM27.3 million yet to be recognised and expected to be delivered by February 2027, providing near-term revenue visibility.
The firm said United Asiapac aims to grow its revenue by securing more contracts from existing and new upstream operators, supported by its expanded equipment fleet, experienced technical workforce and comprehensive Petronas and Petros licences.
It added that greater equipment ownership would enhance service responsiveness and reduce turnaround times, strengthening the company's competitive position while supporting higher margins.

Title: Kelington unit to build US$29.3mil air separation unit plant in India
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kelington Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Ace Gases Technologies Pte Ltd will construct a 300 tonnes per day merchant air separation unit (ASU) plant worth US$29.3 million (RM120 million) in Maharashtra, India.
The integrated engineering solutions provider said an ASU plant is an industrial facility that separates atmospheric air into its primary component gases, such as nitrogen, oxygen, and argon.
It said these gases serve as critical inputs across a wide range of industries, including medical oxygen, electronics, healthcare, metallurgy, chemicals, automotive, pharmaceuticals, food processing, engineering and other manufacturing activities.
"The ASU plant will be developed as a standalone merchant plant on a site spanning approximately 20,000 square metres, enabling Kelington to serve a broad base of industrial gas customers across Maharashtra and neighbouring markets.
"The development will also include the supporting infrastructure, utilities, storage facilities and distribution systems required for the production and supply of industrial gases," the group said in a statement.
Kelington said the development works are expected to commence in August 2026 and are targeted for completion by the third quarter of 2028.
It said the investment will be funded through a combination of internally generated funds and bank borrowings.
Kelington chief executive officer Lim Seng Chuan said that by establishing a local ASU plant, the group will be well-positioned to capture rising demand from customers seeking reliable, locally available industrial gases.
Maharashtra is one of India's leading industrial states, supported by a sizeable manufacturing base.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's Q2 2026 GDP growth accelerates to 5.29pct
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.29 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) in the second quarter of 2026, driven mainly by manufacturing on the production side and household consumption on the expenditure side.
Statistics Indonesia (BPS) National Accounts and Statistical Analysis deputy M Edy Mahmud said GDP at current prices reached 6,552.1 trillion rupiah (1 million rupiah = RM227.10), while GDP at constant prices stood at 3,576.2 trillion rupiah.
"The Indonesian economy in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026 grew 5.29 per cent y-o-y, and this growth was higher than the 5.12 per cent recorded in Q2 2025," he told a press conference on Wednesday.
M Edy said the economy also grew 3.73 per cent quarter-on-quarter, while cumulative growth in the first half of 2026 reached 5.45 per cent compared with the corresponding period last year.
From the production side, he said manufacturing remained the largest source of growth, contributing 0.90 percentage points after expanding 4.52 per cent y-o-y and accounting for 18.50 per cent of GDP.
"On the expenditure side, household consumption was the largest contributor to economic growth, growing 5.06 per cent y-o-y, contributing 2.67 percentage points to growth, and accounting for 53.32 per cent of GDP," he said.
M Edy said gross fixed capital formation contributed 2.06 percentage points to economic growth, while government consumption contributed 1.07 percentage points, whereas net exports subtracted 0.78 percentage points.
He said all business sectors recorded positive y-o-y growth in the second quarter except mining.
"Trade activity was driven by higher distribution of goods due to increased supplies from the agriculture and manufacturing sectors as well as imports, along with stronger sales of cars and motorcycles, particularly commercial vehicles," he said.
M Edy added that trade contributed 0.83 percentage points to overall economic growth, followed by construction at 0.62 percentage points and information and communication at 0.48 percentage points.

Title: Viral e-rider dispute at BPoint not on MBJB land, says city council
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) has clarified that a viral altercation involving an e-rider selling packet drinks at BPoint occurred on privately-owned property.
The clarification came after a video circulated on social media showing the e-rider being pushed by a foreigner who allegedly claimed the area belonged to him.
In a statement, MBJB said checks found that the location shown in the video, including the parking area where the incident occurred, was privately owned and not administered or managed by the council.
MBJB said it issues business licences to traders operating at BPoint, with all licences registered under Malaysian citizens.
It added that enforcement action would be taken against unlicensed traders.
Based on preliminary information received by the council, the incident is believed to have occurred after the mobile vendor entered the private property without the owner's permission.
MBJB also said it had obtained another recording showing the full sequence of events and urged the public not to draw conclusions based solely on the viral clip circulating online.
The council added that any allegations involving assault or acts that could cause injury should be reported to police.
BPoint is a popular food and retail hotspot along Jalan Storey, located less than 2km from the Sultan Iskandar Building.
Its proximity to the Malaysia-Singapore land checkpoint makes it a frequent stop for Singaporean motorists entering Johor Baru.

Title: East Asian LNG prices edge higher on heat, geopolitical risk: Rystad Energy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The East Asian liquefied natural gas (LNG) price for October delivery edged up 0.4 per cent week-on-week to US$20.4 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) on Aug 3, as geopolitical risk and extreme heat continued to support spot demand, according to Rystad Energy.
In its Gas and LNG Market Update report, Rystad Energy noted that buying interest has expanded even though prices remain close to the US$20 per MMBtu mark.
Bangladesh is looking to acquire three cargoes for August, following the return of the Excellence LNG floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) after it was shut down due to a fire in mid-July. Additionally, India, Thailand, and Taiwan (China) are also active in the market.
Rystad Energy, which is an independent energy research and business intelligence company headquartered in Oslo, Norway, said Japan and South Korea face a 60 to 70 per cent probability of above-average temperatures in August, raising the prospect of faster inventory drawdowns and additional near-term procurement.
In Japan, the restart of Chugoku Electric's 820-megawatt Shimane 2 nuclear reactor has been delayed from Aug 6 to Aug 19, with the extended outage should increase reliance on gas-fired generation during the heatwave and could add to utilities' LNG requirements, said Rystad Energy.
Meanwhile, the report said in southern China, heavy rainfall following a typhoon in Guangdong province has lowered temperatures and boosted hydropower output, which should reduce cooling demand and limit gas-fired generation, tempering the broader regional tightening.
Rystad Energy analyst for Gas and LNG Research, Antonia Syn, said gas markets are being pulled in two directions at the moment, balancing weather-driven demand against escalating geopolitical risks.
"While President Donald Trump has shelved planned strikes on Iran in favour of renewed diplomatic efforts, last week's attack on LNG carrier Gas Log Shanghai and a drone strike on Egypt's Damietta LNG export terminal demonstrate how quickly supply risks can materialise.
"With Iran denying that talks with the US are underway, markets are unlikely to gain much confidence, leaving sentiment highly sensitive to further geopolitical developments," she said.
According to the report, the disruption in Egypt has reduced the country's direct LNG import nameplate capacity to around 1.4 million tonnes per month, below its July LNG imports of nearly 1.6 million tonnes, capping its regasification capacity and flexibility at a time when LNG imports are particularly important for meeting summer gas demand.
In the United States, Henry Hub prices remained broadly flat over the past week, edging up 0.3 per cent to US$2.77 per MMBtu (on Aug 3). This was attributed to hotter weather and rising power-sector demand offsetting strong supply and weaker LNG feedgas consumption.

Title: China complains to Japan over defence white paper
Article:
BEIJING: China's foreign ministry on Wednesday said it had complained to Japan about Tokyo's newly released defence white paper, accusing it of playing up a Chinese threat and making "unwarranted comments" about Taiwan.
The annual Japanese report, released on Tuesday, claims that China has intensified its military activities around Taiwan, the island Beijing claims as its own territory despite Taipei's rejection.
The paper states that the "overall military balance between China and Taiwan is rapidly tilting in China's favour."
In a response to Reuters regarding the white paper, China's foreign ministry said Tokyo has no right to comment on the Taiwan issue as it is purely China's internal affair.
"How to resolve the Taiwan issue is a matter for the Chinese people themselves and brooks no interference from the Japanese side," the ministry said, adding that China's relevant military activities are legitimate and reasonable.
Ties between Japan and China sank to their ​worst level in years after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in November that Japan could deploy its Self-Defence Forces if any Chinese attack on Taiwan also threatened Japan's survival, with Beijing demanding that she retract what it called an "egregious" remark.
Japan's government is portraying its accelerating military buildup not only as a way to protect the country but as a route to greater prosperity, arguing in the white paper that arms production can support economic growth.
China has accused Japan of accelerating its remilitarisation push instead of reflecting on its history of aggression.
"We urge Japan to stop seeking excuses for military expansion, and refrain from going further down the wrong path," the Chinese foreign ministry said, urging the international community to curb Tokyo's buildup.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Tabung Haji-linked firm's ex-CFO questioned for second day by MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission today continued recording the statement of the former chief financial officer of a government-linked company as part of its investigation into the alleged abuse of power involving the RM370 million acquisition of shares in two plantation companies.
The session, held at the MACC headquarters here, lasted more than six hours.
However, the company's former chief executive officer, who was also scheduled to assist in the investigation, did not turn up due to health reasons.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the former CFO arrived at the commission's headquarters about 10.30am.
"Today marks the second day of the statement taking process after he was released yesterday.
"The statement recording is being continued to complete investigations arising from the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Tabung Haji. The session concluded about 5pm," he said.
Halim said the former CFO has been instructed to return to MACC headquarters at 10am tomorrow for the continuation of the statement recording.
Yesterday, MACC arrested the
former CEO and former CFO of the compan
y after they gave statements in connection with alleged abuse of power.
Both of them, aged 68 and 60 respectively, were later released on health grounds pending further investigations.
They are suspected of abusing their positions in the acquisition of shares in two plantation companies worth RM370 million.

Title: World faces fresh food price surge, FAO warns
Article:
FRANKFURT: The world is on the verge of another bout of food inflation as wars in Iran and Ukraine along with El Nino create a perfect storm of higher costs and lower crop yields, the chief economist of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation said.
Food prices were a key driver of the 2022 global inflation surge but have been relatively benign so far this year, even tempering in some places the surge caused by high energy costs.
This calm is likely to be temporary, however, as higher crude oil prices, the loss of fertiliser from the Gulf region, the shortage of diesel in some parts of the world and extreme weather are feeding through to costs and will show up in consumer prices, even if with a delay.
"I expect that commodity prices will start to increase more now ... and food prices will start increasing by the end of the year, and next year for sure they will increase more," Maximo Torero told Reuters in an interview.
"The transmission from the commodity to the final food price is around three to six months," he said.
Although some commodity prices, such as wheat, maize and rice
have increased in recent months, most still reflect relatively good harvests, rather than likely difficulties in the coming year.
"The Strait of Hormuz is a problem that affects all the inputs of agricultural commodities, agricultural systems," Torero said.
"Brent oil, because it's used for pumping, packaging, processing, and transportation. And natural gas because it's used for fertilisers."
Meanwhile the damage inflicted by Ukraine on Russia's oil and gas infrastructure curtails the export market for diesel and natural gas, both of them key inputs in food production.
Since commodity prices are global, this inflicts pain across the world, even if richer countries have more cash to buffer producers.
"You're hearing this in Europe, in the US, Brazil and in Asia," Torero said. "Tight margins are putting stress in planting decisions."
Indeed, even in the US, which is self-sufficient for most key inputs, without federal assistance farmers growing nine principal crops may lose US$32 billion in 2027, the American Farm Bureau Federation, an industry lobby group, said.
On a per-acre basis, every crop analysed is projected to remain below breakeven in 2027, it said.
Global wheat and corn planting was already cut in the first three months of the Iran war and some US producers have shifted to soybeans, because they require lower fertiliser inputs.
Australia, one of the world's top crop exporters, recently said that winter crop production is seen down by 21 per cent in part because of a significant increase in both fuel and fertiliser prices and uncertainty over the availability of key inputs.
Meanwhile this year's El Nino weather phenomenon is likely to be especially strong, significantly shifting rainfall patterns, likely impacting commodity prices and potentially pushing tens of millions into acute food insecurity.
The monsoon in India is already delayed and below-average rainfall is seen this month, a potential hit for rice production that could impact global commodity costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-G must explain Nicky Liow's DNAA, say NGOs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A group of civil society organisations has called on Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar to publicly explain the decision to discontinue the money-laundering case against businessman Nicky Liow.
They said Liow had faced 26 charges involving more than RM36 million under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
They said Liow's lawyer had confirmed that a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) was granted and his client was released on June 15, 2023, after the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) accepted a representation on his behalf.
"More than three years on, the A-GC has offered no public account of why that representation was accepted, what considerations informed the decision, or whether the charges will ever be reinstated," the NGOs said in a joint statement today.
The group said the issue was not the outcome of the case, but transparency, adding that the public was entitled to know why a RM36 million money-laundering prosecution was discontinued.
The public is entitled to know why a RM36 million money-laundering prosecution was discontinued, rather than to learn of it, years later, only through a defence press conference, they said.
The groups said the Liow case did not stand alone, claiming it reflected a pattern where serious corruption and money-laundering prosecutions were discontinued through DNNAs without public explanations.
The NGOs said the Madani government's commitment to fighting corruption would be judged by what happened to charges after they were filed, not merely by their filing.
"A pattern in which high-profile corruption and money-laundering cases are quietly discontinued and eventually lapse into full acquittal, without ever being explained or tested at trial, is not accountability," they said.
The groups also maintained that separating the offices of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor alone would not resolve the issue.
They said the power to discontinue prosecutions, whether through a DNAA or accepted representations, would remain unless accompanied by mechanisms to ensure transparency and accountability.
They called for statutory guidelines governing prosecutorial discretion, mandatory written reasons for discontinuing high-profile cases and annual reports disclosing statistics on discontinued prosecutions, reasons and eventual outcomes.
"We have proposed that such a mechanism form part of the Enabling Act and come into force concurrently with the constitutional amendment itself, so that this reform changes not only who holds prosecutorial discretion, but how that discretion is exercised, explained and reviewed," they said.
The CSOs called on the A-GC to publicly disclose the basis, considerations and timeline behind the
DNAA granted to Liow
, as well as its intentions regarding the outstanding charges.
They also urged the Parliamentary Special Select Committee and Parliament to ensure that the enabling Act required to operationalise the separation of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor includes statutory guidelines on prosecutorial discretion and annual reporting requirements.
"Separation without this safeguard risks becoming a change in form without a change in substance," they said.
The statement was endorsed by:
1. Project Stability and Accountability for Malaysia (Projek SAMA)
2. The Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (IDEAS)
3. Rasuah Busters
4. The Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (BERSIH)
5. Centre to Combat Corruption & Cronyism (C4 Centre)
6. Pertubuhan IKRAM Malaysia (IKRAM)
7. CSO Platform for Reform
8. Citizens International
9. Pusat KOMAS
10. Saya Anak Bangsa Malaysia (SABM)
11. Agora Society Malaysia
12. Transparency International Malaysia
13. Monitoring Sustainability of Globalisation (MSN)
14. PurpleLily Social Association
15. LLG Cultural Development Centre
16. Allied Coordinating Council of Islamic NGOs (ACCIN) Malaysia
17. KLSCAH Civil Rights Committee (KLSCAH-CRC)

Title: SCIB bags Sabah school rebuilding job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has secured a RM24.59 million engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) subcontract for the reconstruction of the dilapidated Sekolah Kebangsaan Kaingaran in Tambunan, Sabah.
Belian Juta Sdn Bhd awarded the contract to SCIB's wholly-owned subsidiary SCIB Industrialised Building System Sdn Bhd (SIBS).
Under the subcontract, SIBS will undertake the execution, performance and completion of the reconstruction works, including supplying all necessary materials, machinery, equipment, mechanical plants and labour.
The project is scheduled to commence on Aug 10, 2026, and is expected to be completed by Jan 22, 2029, providing the group with earnings visibility over a 29-month execution period.
The latest contract further strengthens SCIB's construction and EPCC project pipeline in Sabah, while reinforcing its track record in delivering public sector education infrastructure projects.
Chairman Datuk Chong Loong Men said the contract reflects the continued confidence placed in SCIB's project execution capabilities within Sabah's public infrastructure sector.
"Education infrastructure plays a vital role in supporting community development, and we are honoured to contribute to creating a safer and more conducive learning environment through the reconstruction of Sekolah Kebangsaan Kaingaran."
He added: "Sabah continues to offer attractive opportunities, driven by ongoing investments in education, public infrastructure and community facilities."
The contract is expected to contribute positively to SCIB's earnings over the duration of the project, with revenue and profit recognised progressively based on completed work.
The project will be funded through internally generated funds and/or project progress billings, allowing the company to align funding requirements efficiently with implementation.

Title: Kedah family's disappearance may be linked to 'kutu' debts
Article:
JITRA: Police have not ruled out "kutu" debts as a possible reason behind the disappearance of a family of three from Taman Desa Bayanmas in Bukit Kayu Hitam.
Kubang Pasu police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said police had received a report against the wife from a person claiming to be a victim of the scheme.
He said the couple and their child remained missing, adding that immigration checks showed no record of them leaving the country.
"Investigations are ongoing, and we urge members of the public to contact us if they have any information.
"We are investigating all angles, including the possibility that they fell victim to a crime or were involved in an accident," he said when contacted.
The matter came to light after the woman's 62-year-old father lodged a police report yesterday after failing to trace his daughter, son-in-law and grandchild.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Justice for Rocky: Animals lovers rally in front of Klang council office
Article:
KLANG: Some 200 animal lovers and activists gathered outside the Klang Royal City Council (MBDK) demanding justice for Rocky, the dog which died during an enforcement operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah last week.
The peaceful protest saw several participants bringing along their pet dogs, while passing motorists repeatedly honked their horns in a show of solidarity with the demonstrators.
The gathering came days after a video went viral showing Rocky's owner pleading with enforcement officers to release the dog.
The footage also captured a struggle between the owner and an enforcement officer before the dog was dragged, later dying at the scene.
Rocky's death has ignited nationwide outrage over the treatment of stray animals and the standard operating procedures (SOP) employed by local authorities.
The incident prompted widespread condemnation from the public, animal welfare groups and members of the royal family.
Holding placards calling for accountability and humane reforms, the protesters alleged that enforcement officers had failed to comply with existing SOPs for capturing stray dogs, resulting in Rocky's death.
Global Human Rights Federation (GHRF) president Shashi Kumar said the tragedy reflected a much larger failure by the government to address the country's long-standing stray animal problem.
"This issue has existed since the early 1980s, yet successive governments have failed to implement a permanent and humane solution. The response has always been the same, catch, shoot or euthanise stray animals. That is not a solution," he told reporters.
Shashi said non-governmental organisations, rescuers and animal feeders had long advocated a nationwide trap-neuter-return (TNR) programme, arguing that sterilisation was the most effective way to control the stray population.
He said the groups had submitted numerous proposals and memorandums to the Housing and Local Government Ministry, including after a meeting with ministry officials on March 4, 2025, but claimed their proposals were rejected on the grounds that there was insufficient funding.
"We even submitted a working paper together with the estimated budget, but we were told there was no money. Yet the government continues to spend resources on catching and killing stray animals instead of addressing the root cause.
"Countries such as Japan, Australia and New Zealand have adopted humane and scientific methods through sterilisation programmes. Why can't Malaysia do the same?
"The government should subsidise neutering at its veterinary clinics. It costs between RM300 and RM350 to neuter a dog, which is beyond the means of many people, especially those in the B40 group."
Shashi said animal feeders, rescuers and volunteers, regardless of race or religion, had been bearing the cost of sterilising stray animals without government assistance.
He also criticised local councils for allegedly imposing fees of between RM1,000 and RM2,000 for owners to reclaim impounded dogs, describing the practice as exploitative.
He questioned educational materials produced by the ministry, claiming they portrayed stray dogs as inherently dangerous and fostered fear instead of encouraging humane population management.
On Rocky's death, Shashi claimed the officers involved did not use the proper equipment prescribed under the SOP.
"The issue is not whether Rocky was owned or a stray. The issue is how he was captured. From the video, it appeared that a wire cable was used instead of the approved equipment.
"Anyone tasked with capturing stray animals should undergo proper training and certification," he said.
He also criticised MBDK's explanation that it lacked sufficient manpower and had relied on members of the public during enforcement operations.
"If enforcement requires specialised training, how can untrained members of the public be expected to assist? By that logic, would the police ask members of the public to help arrest criminals because they do not have enough personnel?"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia steps up disinformation campaigns ahead of German elections, security sources say
Article:
BERLIN: Russia is intensifying disinformation campaigns in Germany, German security sources told Reuters, ahead of state elections in which the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) appears set to make major gains.
Germany is holding elections in Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania next month.
Polls suggest the AfD, whose leader has vowed to upend the political consensus and restore German ties with Russia — largely frozen due to Moscow's war in Ukraine — could win a majority and even take power in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
The Russian campaigns aim to polarise the political climate and discredit the governing conservative CDU party and its coalition partner, the SPD, as well as the Greens and Free Democratic Party, the sources said.
Russia's embassy in Berlin did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Moscow has consistently denied involvement in disinformation campaigns against the West.
The four security sources, who asked not to be named as they were not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, said German authorities are certain the campaigns are being centrally orchestrated from Russia using a number of companies.
The campaigns are using social media to disseminate videos, mainly in English, bearing the logos of reputable media outlets including the BBC and German broadcaster ARD.
They contain false accusations against local politicians, ranging from allegations of embezzlement to sexual harassment and abuse.
Moscow has regularly faced accusations of election interference.
The German government warned of a similar Russian-orchestrated disinformation campaign ahead of federal parliamentary elections last year.
And recently, Russia was accused of seeking to influence elections in Moldova and Armenia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nanta: LPT2 concessionaire to review long-term safety measures after elephant collision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The concessionaire of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) has been instructed to immediately repair the damaged safety fence and review long-term measures to enhance safety following a collision involving a vehicle and a herd of elephants at Km274.6 northbound along the Cheneh-Chukai stretch last night.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said an inspection at the site found that the existing safety fence had collapsed, believed to have been damaged after being struck by the herd of elephants passing through the area.
"The technical team is already on site to assess the extent of the damage and coordinate the repair works as soon as possible. I have been informed that the repair works will begin no later than tomorrow (Aug 6, 2026)," he said in a post on X today.
As an initial preventive measure, he said the LPT2 concessionaire has also been instructed to increase the frequency of patrols, particularly at night, in high-risk areas to monitor wildlife movement and ensure the safety of highway users.
He said the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) has also been directed to hold discussions with the LPT2 concessionaire and the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) to identify more effective long-term solutions.
Apart from wildlife mitigation measures, Nanta said he has also instructed that a proposal to improve lighting in high-risk areas, including the installation of LED lights, be studied to assess its suitability and the need for its implementation.
He said the incident is being taken seriously as it not only involved the safety of highway users but also reflected the growing challenge of managing human-wildlife conflict.
He also expressed sympathy to the two people injured in the accident and advised highway users to remain vigilant, observe speed limits and exercise extra caution, particularly when travelling through areas identified as wildlife crossing routes.
Yesterday, a husband and wife were reported injured after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they
were travelling in collided
with a herd of elephants crossing the LPT2.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rocky's death sparks probe into dog-catching SOP
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The owner of Rocky, a pet dog allegedly beaten to death during an attempt to catch stray dogs in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, has called for a transparent investigation into the incident.
S. Roghini Devi, 42, said she returned home on July 29 and found Rocky restrained with a snare around his neck.
She said she repeatedly pleaded for the snare to be released and offered to hand the dog over, but those present refused.
Roghini also alleged that she was struck with a wooden stick when she tried to free Rocky, while her child was prevented from cutting the snare.
"Klang Royal City Council officers arrived about five to 10 minutes later, by which time Rocky was unresponsive," she said during a press conference in Petaling Jaya today.
She described Rocky as a beloved family pet that had been part of the family since August 2024, showing photographs of the dog with her children and playing inside their home since he was a puppy.
Roghini said she was awaiting the veterinary report from the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and a full police investigation.
"I am waiting for the DVS report so justice can follow," she said.
Meanwhile, the Stray Animals Foundation of Malaysia (SAFM) has urged authorities to clarify whether proper procedures were followed during the operation that led to Rocky's death.
SAFM president Kalaivanan Ravichandran said the group received a complaint from Roghini through its official WhatsApp channel on July 30 and has been assisting her since.
"We are not here to decide who is guilty or to pre-empt legal processes.
"That matter must be assessed using original footage, witness statements, physical evidence, formal veterinary examination and proper legal procedures," he said.
Kalaivanan said Rocky's body had been handed over to the Selangor DVS for veterinary examination and an official investigation, adding that the group would continue to monitor the progress of the probe.
He said while pet owners are responsible for licensing and controlling their animals, the absence of a licence did not justify causing unnecessary pain or suffering.
"Lack of a licence does not give anyone the right to inflict unnecessary pain and suffering on an animal," he said.
Kalaivanan also called on MPK to clarify whether the operation was an official council action and provide details including the complaint or operation reference number, authorising officer, names and roles of those involved, training records, equipment used and the incident report.
"Who captured and handled Rocky — officers or contractors? Were they appointed, trained and supervised? Under what authority did they enter private property? What device was used on Rocky's neck?" he asked.
He urged the DVS and police to investigate the case transparently and look beyond the viral video for aspects of the incident that require further scrutiny.
On Aug 2, the DVS lodged a police report and recorded statements from several individuals as part of its investigation into the alleged abuse of Rocky, which was captured in a video.
The DVS said its Animal Welfare Team filed the report after receiving the carcass of a male dog believed to be Rocky, following the circulation of a video showing several individuals tying and pulling the dog by its neck while a woman pleaded for it to be released.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher found dead in school toilet in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: A 55-year-old teacher was found dead inside a toilet at SMK Bau along Jalan Sebuku in Bau this morning.
Wong Lee Choo was found unconscious on the toilet floor and later pronounced dead.
Bau police chief Superintendent Mohd Haide A. Rahman said Wong had served as a Science and Biology teacher at SMK Bau for about 25 years.
Haide said a colleague last saw her at 8.15am in the teachers' room, shortly before she said she was going to the toilet.
At 8.35am, another teacher realised that Wong had not arrived for class and asked a colleague to check the toilet.
"Upon opening the toilet door, the victim was found lying unconscious," he said.
Emergency services were called, and a medical officer later pronounced her dead.
Haide said there were no suspicious injuries on Wong and no elements of foul play were found at the scene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police submit investigation paper on Rocky's death to DPP
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The investigation paper into the death of a dog, known as Rocky, during a stray dog-catching operation on July 29 has been submitted to the deputy public prosecutor's office.
South Klang police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey confirmed the matter, saying the report was submitted yesterday.
"The investigation paper on Rocky's case was referred to the deputy public prosecutor's office yesterday. We are still awaiting further instructions," he said briefly today.
Previously, police opened an investigation paper into the dog's death under Section 428 of the Penal Code.
Further investigations into the incident are believed to have found elements of cruelty towards an animal.
Lim said the dog was confirmed dead in the incident, which occurred at about 10.50pm on July 29 in front of a house at Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang.
Police also gave full assurance that investigations into the dog's death during the stray dog-catching operation by the Klang Royal City Council (MBDK) would be conducted fairly, transparently and professionally.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar orders HR Ministry to fast-track first 15,000 foreign worker applications
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Human Resources Ministry to immediately process 15,000 foreign worker applications to meet urgent manpower needs in key sectors.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet took note of ongoing recruitment issues during its weekly meeting today.
"The prime minister has asked the Human Resources Ministry to immediately process the first 15,000 foreign worker applications.
"This is to meet workforce requirements in the sectors involved and directly support economic activities in the country," he told a post-cabinet press briefing.
On July 6, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that the ministry had assumed full control over
foreign worker quota management
following a cabinet directive on July 1.
Ramanan said the consolidation aimed to strengthen recruitment governance while ensuring industry manpower needs are met efficiently and systematically.
As of July 6, the ministry had received 22,476 quota applications involving 548 companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perhilitan tracking elephant herd after  LPT2 MPV collision
Article:
CHUKAI: The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is tracking a herd of wild elephants that was hit by a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) at Km274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near the Cheneh Toll Plaza interchange, last night.
State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the department is using drones to monitor the location and movements of the herd in the vicinity of the accident site.
He said the elephants are believed to have emerged from the Bukit Bandi Forest Reserve, located about 8km from the scene of the accident.
Dennis said six Perhilitan personnel were deployed to the accident site from 12.30am today to carry out monitoring and control operations, including in the surrounding Cheneh area.
"The operation is aimed at determining the herd's location and movements, while ensuring the safety of highway users," he told Bernama today.
He said Perhilitan would also take the necessary action if the herd was found to be still in the vicinity of the highway.
He also advised motorists not to panic if they encountered wild elephants, but instead to avoid approaching them or throwing objects at the animals, as this could provoke them.
Motorists are also advised not to sound their horns, use high beams or flash their headlights at the elephants to avoid making the animals feel threatened or behave aggressively.
"Motorists are also urged to give the elephants enough space to cross safely and maintain a safe distance to avoid any untoward incidents," he said.
Earlier, Bernama reported that a husband and wife were injured after the MPV they were travelling in
collided with a herd of wild elephants
at the location at 10.20pm last night.
Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said in the incident, Abdul Wahid Ismail, 55, sustained minor injuries to his left hand, while his wife, Fauziah Muda, 52, injured her right hand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil police probe plot to carry out election attacks
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazilian security officials said Tuesday they were investigating eight suspects of plotting on Telegram to carry out attacks in the capital during October's elections, in which President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is seeking a fourth term.
Intercepted communications showed the suspects, aged 19 to 31, were planning "severe acts of violence" against the presidential palace, parliament, Supreme Court and various ministries in Brasilia, said Victor Fernandes, digital rights secretary with the justice ministry.
He told a press conference that the suspects were members of "two public groups on the Telegram platform that shared information regarding the planning of attacks in Brasilia" during the election period.
They were conspiring against "the political system as a whole, without specifying left or right" and without targeting specific officials by name, said Maurilio Coelho, head of intelligence for the Brasilia civil police.
They are from five different states, do not know each other personally and do not have criminal records, Coelho said. One of them is a seminarian at a monastery in northeastern Pernambuco.
According to a police statement, the group had exchanged messages about travelling to Brasilia, storming buildings, choosing targets, recruiting people from different states, and conducting tactical training.
They also allegedly shared building plans and 3D models of government buildings in the capital, as well as "manuals for the manufacture of explosive devices."
The investigation was triggered by information from a cybercrimes intelligence unit.
Police have seized electronic devices and are investigating how organised the group was and how far any plans had progressed.
Authorities have asked the National Data Protection Agency – an independent public body – to investigate whether Telegram failed in its duty to "prevent the mass circulation of criminal content," said Fernandes.
In April, Brazil passed a law tightening regulations regarding the liability of digital platforms and social networks for content shared by their users.
In the Oct 4 presidential election, Lula will face off against right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.
The 71-year-old former leader is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup after losing a re-election bid in 2022.
Hundreds of Jair Bolsonaro's supporters were convicted over the January 2023 storming of government buildings and the Supreme Court in Brasilia, a week after Lula took office.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Passport-forging syndicate mastermind among three arrested in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has arrested the alleged mastermind behind a passport-forging syndicate in Kuala Lumpur, said Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban.
The syndicate's modus operandi was to offer services to foreigners in the Klang Valley who wanted to undergo foreign worker health screening (Fomema) but had failed the examination or were deemed unfit.
"The forged passports were amended or modified to enable them to be used during the health screening process.
"A fee ranging from RM80 to RM130 was charged for each passport.
"This marks the fifth arrest involving syndicates using the same modus operandi, and this particular syndicate has been operating since the beginning of the year," Zakaria said in a statement today.
The Indonesian man, believed to be the mastermind, was arrested under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passports Act 1966 for unlawful possession, control or retention of travel documents.
The operation was conducted at Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Bukit Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, at 11pm.
"Based on public information and a one-month intelligence gathering effort, the operations team was deployed to residential premises and detained one Indonesian man believed to be the mastermind, another Indonesian man and an Indonesian woman believed to be syndicate members.
"Initial checks revealed that the detained mastermind holds a Temporary Employment Visit Pass for the construction sector, while the other foreigners were found to have overstayed," he said.
All detained foreigners, aged between 30 and 50, have been taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action.
The department seized 119 passports believed to be forged — comprising 85 Indonesian passports, seven Bangladeshi passports, 22 Myanmar passports, two Vietnamese passports, one Nepalese passport and two Indian passports.
It also seized a printer, mobile phones and RM1,500 in cash believed to be proceeds from unlawful activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Social media platforms told to automate scam, gambling content takedowns
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Social media platforms must prepare their systems for automatic takedown of identified scam and online gambling content to comply with online safety regulations.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move was necessary to ensure platforms comply with the Child Protection Code (CPC) and Risk Mitigation Code (RMC) issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
He said platforms had previously indicated their willingness to comply but needed time to align their internal mechanisms.
"We have given them time. MCMC has issued the CPC and RMC under the Online Safety Act.
"These two codes will ensure platforms comply with online safety regulations, including those relating to scam and online gambling content," he said at the post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today.
Fahmi said automated takedowns had become increasingly important as MCMC's removal requests, particularly involving scams and online gambling, had surpassed last year's total.
He said the increase had strained MCMC's resources, with each takedown request requiring about 30 minutes of work by its personnel.
The situation was further complicated by the repetitive nature of such content, with many scam and online gambling posts using nearly identical images, videos and wording.
"Much of the online gambling and scam content on these platforms is repeated. It uses almost the same images, videos and wording.
"That is why I described it as a waste of MCMC's time, because the content is nearly identical," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RHB unveils Malaysia's first bank-owned unified payment gateway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd has launched RHB Pay, which it describes as Malaysia's first bank-owned unified online payment gateway.
It allows businesses to accept digital payments through a single platform and receive funds directly into their RHB accounts.
Built, owned and operated entirely by RHB, the platform is designed to provide businesses with bank-grade security, automated reconciliation, enhanced cash flow visibility and faster access to funds.
RHB group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Rashid Mohamad said businesses undergoing digital transformation are increasingly seeking payment solutions that offer not only convenience and efficiency, but also greater security, reliability and control over cash flows.
The platform currently supports card payments, FPX and DuitNow Pay through a single integration.
RHB said additional payment capabilities, including e-wallets, QR payments, direct debit and auto debit, are expected to be introduced in the fourth quarter of 2026 under its second phase rollout.
RHB Pay is targeted at mid-sized enterprises, commercial businesses, corporates and government-linked institutions seeking a streamlined and scalable payment acceptance solution.
Through integration with PayNet's payment infrastructure, RHB said the platform enables businesses to participate in the expanding digital economy while providing a secure and seamless payment experience.
PayNet chief executive officer Praveen Rajan said the launch demonstrates how established financial institutions can create new value by responding to evolving customer needs.
"It shows how established financial institutions can unlock new growth opportunities by responding to evolving customer needs and bringing new solutions to the market.
@We are pleased to support this innovation through PayNet's national payment rails," he said.
The launch also marked the start of the RHB Progress Series 2026: Roots Run Wide.
It is the group's flagship thought leadership forum that brings together policymakers and business leaders to discuss Malaysia's economic transformation and future growth opportunities.
It features keynote addresses from Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Rocky's owner mulls legal action after probe outcome
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The owner of Rocky, a dog at the centre of a recent controversy, is considering legal action pending the outcome of ongoing investigations, her legal team said today.
Lawyer Choo Dee Wei, who is representing Rocky's owner S. Roghini Devi, 42, said consultations were under way but any formal legal steps would only be taken after investigators conclude their enquiries.
"We are discussing the matter with her, but it would be done after the outcome of the investigation," he said after a briefing on the incident in Petaling Jaya today.
On Aug 2, the
Department of Veterinary Services (DVS)
lodged a police report and recorded statements from several people as part of its investigation into the alleged abuse of Rocky, which was captured in a video.
The DVS said its Animal Welfare Team filed the report after receiving the carcass of a male dog believed to be Rocky, following the circulation of a video showing several individuals tying and pulling the dog by its neck while a woman pleaded for it to be released.
The operation, carried out from 8.30pm to midnight on July 29, followed complaints from residents over safety concerns linked to an increase in stray dogs in the area.
Choo said the DVS had lodged a police report, but a decision regarding the disposition of the carcass remained unresolved.
He said that his firm was engaged by the Stray Animals Foundation of Malaysia (SAFM), with legal services for the matter being provided pro bono.
Choo also declined to give a firm date for any legal filing, noting that it would depend on manpower availability and the pace of the investigations.
"Because of the optics on this case, we would be putting this as a priority. If there is no response, the team will write (to authorities) for an update," he said.
On possible legal routes, Choo said the team would assess whether standard operating procedures (SOPs) had been followed.
"If municipal procedures were not complied with, a judicial review of the municipal council's actions could be pursued.
"The judicial review would examine how they complied or did not comply with their SOPs," he said.
He said the primary focus would be on Klang Royal City Council if investigators found a connection between the alleged perpetrators and the council.
"If no such link exists, legal action would be taken against those responsible."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Turkish court ordered block of Istanbul Mayor Imamoglu's candidacy account
Article:
ISTANBUL: Social media platform X said on Tuesday it was complying with a Turkish court order to block access in the country to jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu's presidential candidacy office account, but was challenging the order in court.
An Istanbul court ordered X to restrict access to Imamoglu's account, which has around 225,700 followers, to protect national security and public order, according to a copy of the order posted by X.
X said Turkish law required it to implement the restriction, but that it disagreed with the order and had started legal proceedings.
Police detained Imamoglu, President Tayyip Erdogan's main political rival, on March 19, 2025, triggering Turkiye's largest protests in more than a decade.
Imamoglu remains in jail pending trial on charges ranging from graft to espionage and terrorism, which he strongly denies.
Imamoglu was elected as the Republican People's Party's presidential candidate in an internal party vote days after his detention in March 2025.
His university diploma, which is a requirement for being a presidential candidate, was annulled by Istanbul University a day before he was detained.
Imamoglu's main X account, which had nearly 10 million followers, was blocked in Turkiye in May 2025 under a similar order. X also filed a legal challenge against that order, arguing against the restriction.
Under billionaire owner Elon Musk, X has often portrayed itself as a defender of free speech, though the platform says it complies with valid local laws in countries where it operates while seeking to challenge some orders through the courts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: House fire in Sungai Bakap leaves one injured
Article:
SUNGAI BAKAP: A terrace house was 50 per cent destroyed in a fire at Lorong Bakap Permai 9 here today, with one victim reported in the incident.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said an emergency call was received at 2.46pm and a team from the Sungai Bakap station despatched to the scene.
"The fire involved a single-storey terrace house measuring about 70ft by 20ft. Preliminary assessment showed the blaze destroyed about 50 per cent of the house.
"One victim was reported to be involved in the incident. Firefighters immediately carried out firefighting and fire containment operations to prevent the blaze from spreading to adjoining properties," he said in a statement today.
John said the department mobilised a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and a rapid response vehicle, while volunteer fire brigades from Jawi and Valdor arrived about 3pm to assist.
"Firefighting operations are still ongoing and the operation has yet to be concluded. Further information will be released as it becomes available," he added.
The incident has since gone viral with some people claiming it could be due to a gas explosion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Witness claims beatings, electric shocks while under protection programme
Article:
TAWAU: A plaintiff's witness in a RM190 million civil suit involving former senior officers and intelligence personnel of the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) claimed she was beaten, subjected to electric shocks and forced to take pills.
Nurima Juli, 36, made the claims while continuing her testimony at the High Court here today, alleging that the incidents occurred while she was under the Witness Protection Programme.
It was the second day of the hearing of the suit filed against the police and 12 other defendants before Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos.
The witness, who is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence, also alleged that she received threats from police, with the incidents occurring while she was staying at an apartment.
She further claimed she was forced to take blue and white pills, which caused memory problems, including an inability to remember her children.
During cross-examination by Federal Senior Counsel Mardziatun Nisa Ahamadul Kaber, the witness said she could not remember whether she had lodged a police report or undergone a medical examination in relation to the alleged injuries.
Mardziatun suggested that there was no specific police report or hospital medical record confirming physical injuries or signs of electric shocks to her head or body.
In response, the witness said: "I don't remember."
The lawyer also suggested that the witness's claims about "memory-loss medication", "electric shocks to the head" and being detained in an apartment in Putrajaya were stories fabricated by her.
The witness disagreed.
During re-examination by the plaintiff's lawyer, Sharatha Masyaroh John Ridwan Lincon, the witness explained that the absence of police reports or medical records was because she claimed she had been instructed not to lodge a report against the police officers involved.
The witness said she had previously informed the court during a case mention that she had allegedly been beaten while under investigation.
She said she was subsequently asked to make a report about the incident.
However, she alleged that after the case mention proceedings ended, she was taken back to the interrogation room and instructed not to lodge a report against the policemen concerned.
The proceedings would resume with the plaintiffs' third witness. Constable Ika Zaliah Mohamad Akbar, who served as a lock-up sentry at the Tawau district police headquarters was scheduled to testify.
The trial is scheduled to take place over 30 days in stages and involves three civil suits filed by former Esscom officers and intelligence personnel in 2024 and 2025, which were later consolidated to be heard as a single action.
All plaintiffs were previously among eight accused persons who were acquitted and discharged by the Tawau High Court on Jan 25, 2023, of charges of murdering e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu, 61.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Like I died and came back': Malaysian footballer struck by lightning
Article:
TUMPAT: A 22-year-old footballer who survived a lightning strike that killed one player and injured 11 others in Sungai Golok said he felt like he had "died and come back to life".
Recalling the incident, Mohamad Alif Ezzahan Zulkifli said he was standing about 2 metres from the player who died when
lightning struck
.
He said the bolt struck about 10 minutes into the second half of the Golok FA Cup semi-final match, which had kicked off at 4pm Thai time.
"Dark clouds started to gather about an hour later. It was about to rain when strong winds and lightning formed over the field.
"I suddenly fell to the ground and lost consciousness. At first, I thought someone had hit me because only my head was hurting.
"When I regained consciousness, I was only semi-conscious and felt my head spinning badly.
"I remember hearing people around me telling me to recite the syahadah before I lost consciousness again," said the third of seven siblings.
When met at his home in Kampung Tujuh near Pengkalan Kubor today, Alif said that while still dizzy, he saw the victim, a Thai national, lying face-up on the pitch.
"I only knew the victim casually through football, and he was a good player," he added.
Alif was rushed to Sungai Golok Hospital after the lightning strike before being transferred to Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital in Kota Baru for further treatment.
Alif, who previously played for Kelantan FA, was discharged this morning after doctors confirmed he had not suffered serious injuries.
Yesterday's match was only Alif's second appearance for Thai side SAMCOLTS, who were playing against Abu x Nong Sirin at Santiphap Stadium.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man suffers burns in fire that damaged five RAKR houses in Seberang Jerteh
Article:
JERTIH, Aug 5 — Five terraced houses at the Low-Cost Public Housing (RAKR) area in Seberang Jerteh here were damaged, while a man was injured, in a fire that broke out this morning.
Jertih Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Chief Mustafa Ismail said his team received an emergency call at 10.28am and arrived at the location at 11.44am, before successfully controlling the fire about 30 minutes later.
“The fire involved five permanent residential houses, with one house completely destroyed and another almost completely destroyed, while the other three suffered damages ranging between 5 and 50 per cent,” he said.
“A total of 14 firefighters and personnel along with two fire engines from the Jertih and Besut fire stations were involved in the firefighting operation, which utilised water from a nearby fire hydrant. The cause of the fire and the actual amount of losses are still under investigation,” he told reporters at the scene today.
Meanwhile, the victim injured in the incident, Muhammad Rais Rosli, 34, expressed his dismay and sadness over losing RM25,000 in cash that he had saved for a long time, as well as his children’s duit raya (festive money) totaling RM5,000 that had been collected over the past two years.
The furniture store worker suffered burns on his left hand while trying to rescue belongings from his rented house after realising that the fire was beginning to spread.
“No one was at home during the incident because all my children were at school, while I was at work and my wife (Nur Khairunnisa Muhammad Amar, 40) had taken our sick pet cat to a veterinary clinic.
“I was informed about the incident through a phone call from my mother-in-law. After that, I rushed home and tried to extinguish the fire and save our belongings, but my left hand got burned while lifting a hot gas cylinder.
“Not many items could be saved other than a television and a fan, while clothes, the children’s school books, and other things were completely burnt. Now, our family is left with only the clothes on our backs,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: PKR congress to assess party performance in Johor, Negeri Sembilan polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The upcoming PKR national congress is expected to look into the party’s performance in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections and also the federal government’s policies, said PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said that apart from fulfilling the party’s constitutional requirements under the Registrar of Societies (RoS), the congress will be a forum for reflection on the election results in the two states.
“Delegates, especially from Johor and Negeri Sembilan, are expected to share their views and experiences to identify weaknesses and propose improvements for the party.
“Delegates can learn and reflect on these two state elections,” he said during the weekly post-Cabinet media conference that was broadcasted live today.
Fahmi, who is the communications minister and unity government spokesman, said other matters expected to be brought up in the congress are strengthening the party machinery, division of tasks, candidate preparation and strategies to face the upcoming elections.
He said that the congress is also likely to see proposals from delegates regarding improvements to government policies.
The PKR national congress is scheduled to be held on August 16.
Following Pakatan Harapan’s poor showing in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state polls, the congress is expected to be an important platform for PKR to reassess its future.

Title: PM directs Human Resources Ministry to expedite 15,000 foreign worker applications, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) to immediately process the first 15,000 foreign worker applications to address labour shortages in key sectors and support Malaysia’s economic activities.
Communications Minister and Madani Government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move was aimed at meeting workforce demand across affected industries.
“This is to fulfil the labour needs of the sectors concerned and, in turn, support economic activity in the country,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting today.
Prior to this, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that Kesuma had assumed full responsibility for managing the One-Stop Centre (OSC) for Foreign Worker Management with immediate effect, following a Cabinet decision on July 1.
He said the move was intended to strengthen governance in the recruitment of foreign workers while ensuring the labour needs of industry were met more efficiently and systematically.
The decision, made at the first 2026 Cabinet Committee on Foreign Workers meeting on June 30, placed the OSC under Kesuma with immediate effect. — Bernama

Title: Penang Second Bridge eastbound route to Batu Kawan closed Aug 8 night for Cultural Night Run
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — The eastbound route on the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah Bridge (JSAHMS), from Batu Maung to Batu Kawan, will be temporarily closed from 8pm on August 8 until 3am on August 9.
Jambatan Kedua Sdn Bhd (JKSB) said in a statement today that the closure was to facilitate the Cultural Night Run 2026.
However, the westbound route from Batu Kawan to Batu Maung will remain open, as will routes from Bandar Cassia and the Batu Kawan Industrial Park (BKIP) to the North-South Expressway (PLUS).
JKSB advised motorists travelling from Penang island to the mainland during the closure to use the Penang Bridge.
It also urged highway users to comply with traffic signs and instructions throughout the closure to ensure smooth traffic flow and the safety of all road users. — Bernama

Title: Works minister: LPT2 concessionaire to repair fence, review long‑term safety after elephant crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The concessionaire of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) has been instructed to immediately repair the damaged safety fence and review long-term measures to enhance safety following a collision involving a vehicle and a herd of elephants at KM274.6 northbound along the Cheneh-Chukai stretch last night.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said an inspection at the site found that the existing safety fence had collapsed, believed to have been damaged after being struck by the herd of elephants passing through the area.
“The technical team is already on site to assess the extent of the damage and coordinate the repair works as soon as possible. I have been informed that the repair works will begin no later than tomorrow (Aug 6, 2026),” he said in a post on X today.
As an initial preventive measure, he said the LPT2 concessionaire has also been instructed to increase the frequency of patrols, particularly at night, in high-risk areas to monitor wildlife movement and ensure the safety of highway users.
He said the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) has also been directed to hold discussions with the LPT2 concessionaire and the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) to identify more effective long-term solutions.
Apart from wildlife mitigation measures, Nanta said he has also instructed that a proposal to improve lighting in high-risk areas, including the installation of LED lights, be studied to assess its suitability and the need for its implementation.
He said the incident is being taken seriously as it not only involved the safety of highway users but also reflected the growing challenge of managing human-wildlife conflict.
He also expressed sympathy to the two people injured in the accident and advised highway users to remain vigilant, observe speed limits and exercise extra caution, particularly when travelling through areas identified as wildlife crossing routes.
Yesterday, a husband and wife were reported injured after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were travelling in collided with a herd of elephants crossing the LPT2. — Bernama

Title: Immigration busts passport forgery syndicate in KL raids, arrests three, seizes 119 forged passports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) detained three Indonesian nationals, including a man suspected to be the mastermind of a passport forgery syndicate, during operations at two locations around here last night.
Its director-general, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, said that three individuals involved, namely two men and one woman aged between 30 and 50, were detained during operations at 11 pm in Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Bukit Cheras, here.
“Preliminary checks found that the ‘mastermind’ holds a Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS Construction Sector) and that the other foreign nationals have overstayed,” he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said the syndicate offered services to foreigners in the Klang Valley who wanted to undergo foreign worker health screenings but did not pass the examination or were deemed unfit.
According to him, the syndicate will charge RM80 to RM130 for each passport that is forged to be altered or modified for use during the health screening process.
“This is the fifth arrest involving a syndicate that uses the same modus operandi, and this syndicate has been operating since the beginning of the year,” he said.
Zakaria said that his team also seized 119 forged passports believed to be from Indonesia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Vietnam, India and Nepal, as well as a printer, mobile phones, and cash amounting to RM1,500, believed to proceeds from the activities involved.
He also suspected that the syndicate mastermind is believed to have committed an offence under Section 12(1)(f) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while two other foreign nationals are believed to have committed offences under Section 6(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
“All the detained foreign nationals were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to discuss refugee repatriation plan with Myanmar junta, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian government will hold talks with the Myanmar junta over the proposed repatriation of 5,000 refugees to the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the Myanmar junta must also ensure that the refugees would not face any danger before the repatriation process could begin.
“Both Wisma Putra and the Home Ministry are tasked with identifying the 5,000 Myanmar refugees for repatriation.
“As a responsible country, Malaysia will not send them back if these refugees are certain to be harmed or have their lives threatened,” he said at the weekly post-Cabinet media conference, which was broadcast live today.
On July 29, it was reported that the Myanmar junta had agreed to receive 5,000 Myanmar refugees from Malaysia.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the latest development was a positive step towards resolving the Myanmar refugee issue in the country.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said Anwar had instructed the Human Resources Ministry to expedite the processing of 15,000 foreign worker applications to meet workforce needs across various sectors.
He said the latest development was announced during today’s Cabinet meeting to ensure the country’s workforce requirements could be met to support economic growth.

Title: Defence minister on two‑day visit to Hanoi to strengthen Malaysia‑Vietnam defence ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin began a two-day official visit to Vietnam today to strengthen defence cooperation between the two countries.
He said the visit marks his first official trip to Vietnam since being appointed Defence Minister.
Mohamed Khaled, who arrived at Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi, is scheduled to meet Vietnam’s Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Gen Phan Van Giang.
“Malaysia and Vietnam have long enjoyed close defence ties.
“The renewal of the Memorandum of Understanding on defence cooperation in December 2023 reflects the commitment of both countries to further strengthen bilateral relations,” he said in a Facebook post today.
